system.summary: German homophonic substitution in two-digit groups 10-99 (2-7 homophones per letter), with capital-letter signs for digraphs (ch, ei, st, ss, tt, mm, sch, ll, au, ff, ai) and three-digit codes for names and military nouns.
system.sibling_key: none: 176 HCPortal key records of the Marburg key volumes checked; the Sixtinus key (HCPortal key 5, Dec 1635) has the same layout but a different table
system.notes: 89 two-digit groups, about 20 digraph signs, about 45 codes (151 tokens), a few name signs. Single figures are plain numerals.

prior_solution.where: HCPortal marks all ten records Not solved; no edition found

conditions.human_role: Problem posed with /goal from catalogue entry 338, which suggested checking the 1635-52 key sheets first. No target-specific intervention.
tools: homophonic simulated annealing with lang de-1640s

solution.what: Fetched the ten HCPortal records and 18 original scans of HStAM 4 h 1411 through api.hcportal.eu.
Harvested all 176 HCPortal cipher-key records of the Marburg key volumes with their users; no Malsburg key. Keys 5 (Sixtinus 1635), 30, 38 and 49 compared with f. 3.
f. 3 transcribed by hand from 2x line crops (455 groups).
Homophonic annealing of f. 3 alone against de-1640s, with and without a letter-frequency penalty.
Remaining pages transcribed by two agents in the same format (about 9,000 more groups); ff. 30-31 found to duplicate ff. 28-29.
Annealing ff. 3+12+18 (1,575 groups): all four restarts converged on the same key and German text (das ich auch noch nit weiss ... garnisonen ... contributiones vom platten lande).
Letter signs valued from context: N/D ch, Y/G ei, Z/O st, W/P ss, L/A tt, R/C/E/M mm, X/j/J sch, H ll, S/F au, T/B ff, Q ai; single figures are numerals.
Digit table re-annealed and polished over all pages with the signs fixed: 23, 40, 75 corrected; rare groups 14, 17, 20, 33, 85 assigned.
Dictionary-segmentation measure; the same measure on shuffled keys gives 50-58%.
236 unread groups re-checked against the scans: 24 misreads and 2 doubled groups corrected, 210 confirmed as written.
Codes valued from context: 128 Cöln, 130 Hamburg, 188 die Staaten, 253 Regiment, 273 Compagnien (grade I).
f. 12 letter-cipher block: many-to-one and null-allowing annealing in German, Latin, French, Italian and Dutch; periodic IC for periods 1-15; Caesar shifts; HCPortal letter keys 2 and 105.
Web search for an edition of the Malsburg letters (Rommel, LAGIS); none found.
Reading measured: 9,338 of 9,736 cipher tokens in words (95.9%); 193 code/sign tokens open; 97.9% of the non-code text.

outcome.method_basis: The two-digit table was recovered by homophonic annealing of the ciphertext against a 17th-century German model, with no key, crib or decipherment; the letter signs and codes were then valued from context.

parts.label: The ten letters (ff. 3-33)

outcome.fraction_read_source: measure.py over the transcriptions (reading_segmented.txt): 9,736 cipher tokens of the letters, duplicate ff. 30-31 excluded; a token is read when all its letters fall in dictionary words; 193 open code/sign tokens count as unread

gaps.item: letter-cipher block at the foot of f. 12 (531 letters)
gaps.detail: a different system: not the Malsburg key, not a simple, homophonic, Caesar or periodic cipher; no fitting key among the 176 HCPortal key records

gaps.item: about 40 three-digit codes and name signs (193 tokens)
gaps.detail: mostly single occurrences; five valued from context (grade I)

outcome.notes: Malsburg reports from Wesel on garrisons, contributions and recruiting, the siege of Ehrenbreitstein (Hermannstein), Jan de Werth at Cologne, the peace talks at Cologne and Hamburg, and plans with the States General.
